chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who pronounced dhahir with his wife three times. He said: 'He must expiate three times.' I said: 'And if he has intercourse before he expiates?' He said: 'He seeks forgiveness of Allah and holds back until he expiates.'

This does not contradict the preceding narrations, because in his saying (peace be upon him) 'let him hold back until he expiates,' it is not specified that it is the expiation of one or two. And if that is not explicit in its wording, it is permissible that the meaning intended is until he expiates the two expiations. And as for what he narrated:

key_terms.ظَاهَرَ: To pronounce Dhahir, a specific form of irrevocable separation/divorce in Shia fiqh
key_terms.يُكَفِّرُ: He expiates / performs the required expiation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a man who pronounces Dhahir three times and has intercourse before completing the expiations?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration to clarify that three separate Dhahir declarations necessitate three distinct expiations, resolving potential ambiguities in earlier reports. It specifies that if intercourse occurs before the expiations are completed, the husband must seek forgiveness and maintain abstinence until the full obligation is fulfilled, ensuring the rulings remain consistent with established jurisprudence.
